messages:
Sara Kim: Heads up — storage-audit flagged several backup objects in the cold-tier bucket that are stored without SSE headers. Found plaintext artifacts named /tmp/backup-*.tar in the uploader pod logs. Can we triage? cc @encops-bot
Mike Rivera: How many objects and which tenants? any recent deploys to uploader?
Sara Kim: 12 objects across 3 tenants, all within the last 24h. uploader v2.3.1 deployed yesterday. Logs show write to /tmp then PutObject without sse headers.
Priya Shah: Do we have evidence the uploader removed SSE headers, or did lifecycle/replication strip them when moving to cold bucket?
Sara Kim: Bucket settings: primary bucket has default SSE-KMS, but the replication->cold-bucket lifecycle rule has a replication transform that appears to drop metadata. CloudTrail PutObject for the cold-bucket shows no SSE headers.
Mike Rivera: That implies replication/transform component lacks KMS access or is rewriting objects. Immediate actions: stop the lifecycle/replication rule, quarantine cold-bucket to reject new puts, and prevent further migration.
Priya Shah: Agreed. Also: enable S3 data-event logging for both buckets (we're missing object-level PutObject events for the replication account). Need that for forensics.
Sara Kim: On the uploader side, I see tempfile usage: the agent writes a local /tmp file and then does a multipart upload by reading the file. Suggest hotfix to stream directly to multipart to avoid local plaintext.
Mike Rivera: Good call. Can you open a PR for stream-upload and roll to staging?
Sara Kim: PR opened, patch rolling to staging now. Patch sets stream=true and removes tmp write for files < 2GB.
Priya Shah: KMS/RBAC: replication lambda/agent doesn't have kms:Encrypt permissions for the CMK used by the primary bucket. We need a scoped grant: allow kms:GenerateDataKey/kms:Encrypt for replication role with ResourceCondition on the buckets. I'll draft a key policy change and a temporary grant.
Mike Rivera: We should also rotate the CMK usage for affected objects or re-wrap with a new key after we re-encrypt. Prioritize canary re-encrypt first.
Priya Shah: Plan of record: 1) Disable lifecycle rule (Sara) 2) Put restrictive bucket policy on cold-bucket to reject non-SSE uploads (Mike) 3) Enable S3 data events + CloudTrail for both buckets (Mike) 4) Patch uploader to stream (Sara) 5) Create KMS grant for replication role and run canary re-encrypt job under encops account (Priya) 6) Run full re-encrypt for 12 objects and validate integrity (Sara & Mike).
Sara Kim: Forensics notes — collecting manifests/hashes for the 12 objects now and uploading to #incidents.
Priya Shah: Creating incident ticket SEC-2026-118 and will include the playbook steps + a temporary RBAC change for the replication role. Encops will handle re-encrypt.
encops-bot: Incident created: SEC-2026-118 by Priya Shah. Assigned to encops@redwood. SLA: 48h.
Mike Rivera: Quick commands for enabling data events I used earlier:
```
aws cloudtrail put-event-selectors --trail-name prod-trail --event-selectors '[{"ReadWriteType":"All","IncludeManagementEvents":false,"DataResources":[{"Type":"AWS::S3::Object","Values":["arn:aws:s3:::primary-bucket/","arn:aws:s3:::cold-bucket/"]}]}]'
```
Priya Shah: I'll add the KMS grant as a scoped one-liner and attach condition on SourceAccount/SourceBucket. Will post the key policy diff in a minute.
Sara Kim: Rolling patch to uploader landed in staging; will monitor logs for further /tmp writes.
Mike Rivera: I'll add the audit query and start searching for other buckets with lifecycle transforms that touch metadata.
Priya Shah: Updating playbook: add a checklist item to block lifecycle transforms that rewrite or strip SSE metadata, and require data-event logging for any replication target.
Sara Kim: thumbs up :+1: I'll coordinate canary re-encrypt once encops grant is in place.
Mike Rivera: Thanks all — marking this Sev2 for now, will update incident ticket with timeline and owners.
